title: The MLOps Lifecycle: Tracking, Registry & Promotion
summary: Why ML systems accumulate hidden technical debt, and the practices that keep them manageable: tracked experiments, reproducible runs, a versioned model registry, and controlled promotion with rollback.
takeaways: Most of a production ML system is code and infrastructure around the model, and that's where debt hides.
Log every run's params, metrics and a reproducibility fingerprint. If it isn't tracked, it didn't happen.
A registry gives models names, versions and stages. Exactly one version serves production.
Promotion should be reversible: keep the previous production version one call away.

steps.label: Train & log
steps.detail: Each run records its params, metrics and a fingerprint of its config.

steps.label: Select
steps.detail: Pick the best run on the agreed metric. Ties go to the earliest, deterministically.

steps.label: Register
steps.detail: Create a new version of the named model from that run.

steps.label: Stage & validate
steps.detail: Move it to Staging, run integration and shadow tests.

steps.label: Promote
steps.detail: Move it to Production. The previous version is archived automatically.

steps.label: Monitor / roll back
steps.detail: Watch live metrics. If they regress, restore the previous version.

terms.definition: Applying DevOps practices (automation, CI/CD, monitoring) to building and operating ML systems.
Recording each training run's parameters, metrics, code version and artifacts so results are comparable and reproducible.
A central store of named, versioned models with lineage to the runs that produced them and lifecycle stages or aliases.
Long-term maintenance cost from shortcuts such as entangled features, glue code, undeclared consumers and pipeline jungles.
Automatically retraining and validating models when new data or triggers arrive (MLOps level 1+).
